visual: Compact bushy evergreen shrub with glossy dark green aromatic leaves, fragrant clusters of small white spring flowers and, when pollinated by a nearby male Skimmia, abundant glossy green berries that ripen vivid red in autumn and persist through winter.
water: Water regularly while establishing and during prolonged dry periods; container plants need more frequent watering. Keep evenly moist but never permanently waterlogged.
soilWarning: No poor dry soil, waterlogging or hot sun
prune: Little pruning required. Remove dead, damaged or badly placed shoots after flowering and lightly shape only when necessary.
toxicity: Fruit are ornamental and should not be eaten; ingestion may cause stomach upset.
resilience: Hardy, slow-growing evergreen that tolerates shade, atmospheric pollution and a degree of neglect once established.
uses: Shady borders, woodland gardens, courtyards, wildlife gardens, winter displays and containers
foliage: Evergreen · glossy dark green aromatic leaves

visual: Elegant clump-forming evergreen fern with erect to arching pinnate fronds, each narrow glossy green leaflet marked by a striking broad creamy-white to silvery central stripe.
water: Keep the compost consistently moist but well drained, allowing little drying between waterings. Appreciates high humidity, especially when grown indoors.
soilWarning: No drought, dry air, wet roots or hot sun
prune: No formal pruning required; cut away old, damaged or browned fronds at the base as necessary.
toxicity: No known hazard; no significant toxicity is widely documented, but the plant is ornamental and not intended for consumption.
hardinessNote: H1C · 5 to 10°C; generally best treated as a houseplant or protected conservatory fern in the UK
resilience: Easy-growing in warm, humid, shaded conditions but vulnerable to frost and excessive drying.
uses: Houseplants, bathrooms, conservatories, terrariums, shaded patios in summer and foliage displays
foliage: Evergreen · green pinnate fronds with broad silvery-white central bands
uncertain: 'Silver Ribbon Fern' is a common/trade name for Pteris nipponica rather than a confirmed cultivar name.
